resolutions.red_first: Watched red on three mutations before it was allowed to be green. (1) The reviewer's own: agent.py `adopted, gap = adopt(si, new_steps)` -> `adopted, gap = (steps[:si] + new_steps, None)` -- red at BOTH `steps = adopted` sites (lines 675 and 1043), because the check follows the alias and `adopted` stops being adopt-derived. (2) A genuine fourth site: `steps = adopt(si, new_steps)[0]` -> `steps = steps[:si] + new_steps` -- red at 1119. (3) In-place: `steps.extend(new_steps)` -- red at 1119 as mutates_steps_in_place. agent.py restored byte-identical after each.
resolutions.fix: `_check_steps_adopt_only` parses src/browser/agent.py with ast and asserts: every Assign whose target is `steps` is either the single first-plan binding (an Await) or adopt-derived -- adopt(...), adopt(...)[i], or a local every one of whose bindings is adopt-derived; no AugAssign/AnnAssign/NamedExpr binds `steps`; no subscript assignment or list-mutating method call on `steps`; and exactly one first-plan binding exists. Read structurally rather than by regex on purpose: the mutation that produced R16 leaves the visible line `steps = adopted` untouched, so a grep for `steps =` sees a linted rebind. Tagged invariant + fast. specs/001-browser-contract.md:225-228 and agent.py's adopt() docstring now name the case instead of asserting the property on convention, and both say plainly that the modal claim stood unenforced for one round (R25) and that this is the same shape as ADR-018's version that R16 falsified.
resolutions.not_covered: adopt() itself could stop calling plan_gap -- a different assertion, graded by observe-drilldown-replan-is-linted, plan-lint-holds-across-a-midrun-replan and plan-gap-truth-table. A future binding through a helper that merely returns adopt()'s value would be red here even though it is safe; deliberate, because a new adoption path should be a human decision.

resolutions.fix: Resolved by taking main's ADR-019 rather than by editing our enumeration: main had independently hit the same defect (its own R21) and fixed it by DELETING both enumerations and publishing one band-source sentence per suite that cites a ledger row by timestamp, graded end to end by published-band-matches-the-ledger's seven items -- including item 3, rule(published) == rule(ledger max), which is exactly what our enumeration violated. Both bands were then re-derived from the merged tree: `fast` 152 cases, ts 20260823-192648, 70.22s, 70.22 x 1.15 = 80.75 -> 85; `invariant` 58 cases, ts 20260823-192533, 13.15s, 13.15 x 1.15 = 15.12 -> 20. Both cited runs are GREEN (152/152 and 58/58) and the ADR says so explicitly, because R21's finding was that the old enumeration published only the red runs. Each band also names the ledger's own maximum at that count (70.38s and 13.80s) and says it derives the same ceiling. The derived 85 is BELOW the committed 90 and does not move it -- section 6's no-ratchet-down rule -- and the ADR states that rather than leaving a reader to reconcile an arrow with the ceiling above it.
